status: partial simulator behavior review; one current PvP card IR call site
findings: Current card IR has one direct Array_Resize call: card_event_semper_fi.OnPlayedFromHand at statement/bytecode offset 1510. It targets the instance integer-ID array cardsToRandom, requests length 8, has no output pins, and is reached only when the deck-derived candidate array exceeds 8 entries.

The installed SDK declares void Array_Resize(const TArray<int32>& TargetArray, int32 Size) in Engine.hpp. The current simulator mutates IList in place, truncates from the tail, zero-fills integer growth, clears at zero, returns null, and leaves the array unchanged for negative sizes.

Existing BotSim tests cover shrink, integer growth, zero, negative-size preservation, void return, and continuation after negative-size invocation in both direct dispatch and VM paths. The existing regression is sufficient; no duplicate test was added.

The negative-size behavior is supported by historical RULE-107 analysis of a prior installed executable (SHA-256 09df6b669944d5ca68f5b56741c05f591c03bfd3600f75829364a3452e661dc0). The currently installed executable has SHA-256 b6f4b6af2af3f9a596182df82abc4e87a2cb51abaff417f558d68e7bbb201305, so the native implementation claim is not current-version revalidation.

The simulator implementation and regression establish local consistency for the exercised element types; they do not establish full Unreal FProperty lifecycle, allocation behavior, or end-to-end Semper Fi card correctness.

verification.existing_regression: Blueprint Array_Resize：原地裁剪/扩容且负长度保留原数组

limitations: Negative-size native semantics come from a historical executable fingerprint and have not been revalidated against the current executable.
The single call-site inventory does not certify Semper Fi or any other card end to end.
Generic reflected-array allocation, destructor/copy operations, and non-integer element semantics were not independently captured in this review.
